title: Granular Billing Canvas — Line-item Token Cost & Pricing Tier Patterns
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Goal: Design a scalable Console view that surfaces line-item token-level costs across routes, models, and pricing tiers, enabling engineers and finance teams to attribute spend, export reconciliations, and apply pricing patterns for bundled and tiered billing.

Scope: prototypes for a dashboard-level 'Billing Canvas' with three primary modes: Overview (aggregated breakdowns), Attribution (per-caller/route/session drilldowns), and Export & Pricing Patterns (CSV/Parquet exports + UI to map routes to price tiers). Include micro-interactions for time-window comparisons, live sampling indicators for large datasets, and an embeddable compact panel for account pages.

Acceptance criteria:
- Show cost per 1k tokens and per-request line-items across model variants and decoders (where available).
- Provide configurable attribution keys: api_key, route, model_version, customer_tag.
- Allow exports filtered by date range and attribution keys into CSV and Parquet with schema including token_type, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, model, route, unit_price_usd, total_cost_usd.
- UI patterns to display tiered pricing (flat, graduated tiers, and committed discounts) and how applied discounts affect unit cost.
- Ensure designs account for slow backend aggregation: display progressive loading and sampling rates, and a control to 'compute full-aggregation' (async job with webhook when finished).

Key trade-offs and decisions:
- Full-line-item pagination vs. sampled aggregation: default to sampled aggregated view for the dashboard to reduce latency; allow on-demand full export for precise reconciliation. This balances UX responsiveness vs. exact accounting.
- Inline pricing editor vs. dedicated pricing modal: opt for a dedicated modal to reduce visual clutter and keep the canvas focused on analysis.
- Show per-token micro-costs to three decimal places; show per-request rounded to cents.

Implementation notes for Eng/PM:
- Backend dependencies: aggregation endpoints (ENG-8123) that return pre-aggregated bucketed counts and a separate export job endpoint (ENG-8340) that writes Parquet to s3.
- Pagination: support cursor-based paginated line-item endpoint for CSV previews.
- Observability: include trace ids for exported jobs and surface cost calculation version (so we can re-run with older schemas).

Design deliverables:
- High-fidelity Figma prototype for Overview, Attribution drilldown, and Export flow (links in attachments).
- Clickable prototype demonstrating: time-compare, tier-visualization, export modal, pricing-rule editor (read-only in this ticket).
- Annotated handoff: component list (table, sparkline, tier-legend, sampling-indicator), accessibility notes (color contrast for tier badges), responsive behavior for narrow consoles.

Open questions:
- Should we support ad-hoc grouping by arbitrary metadata keys emitted in our billing pipeline? (PM leaning: yes but scope separate ticket).
- UX for disputed charges workflows (link to CS ticket flow) — blocked on legal/design alignment.

Next steps:
- Run 2 moderated sessions with Finance and Platform teams (scheduled 2025-01-20 and 2025-01-24).
- Iterate prototype per feedback and hand to Eng for API contract refinement (ENG-8123 owner: Priya Shah).

Notes on uniqueness: This canvas emphasizes the interplay between pricing patterns and token-level attribution and introduces an explicit "compute full-aggregation" async export to avoid sacrificing dashboard responsiveness, a pattern not captured in previous token-focused designs.
